# Owen Ford

## Overview

- **Age:** About thirty or thirty-five years old  <sub>[v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- **Role:** Newspaper man and author  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c24 P27](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0027)</sub>

## Appearance

Owen Ford is tall and broad-shouldered with thick brown hair, a finely-cut nose and chin, and large, brilliant dark-gray eyes that resemble those of his grandmother, Persis Selwyn. He has very well-shaped ears and white teeth that show when he smiles. Unsmiling, his face appears sad and absent-minded, but it lights up with humor and charm when he smiles.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 c23 P9](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0009), [v4 c23 P10](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0010), [v4 c24 P18](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0018), [v4 c24 P21](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0021)_

## Personality

Owen is an artistic, imaginative, and deep-feeling man who appreciates beauty and romance. He possesses an agreeable charm, a pleasant voice, and a delightful smile that quickly wins people over. Though honorable and conscientious enough to suffer in silence rather than compromise a married woman, he possesses strong underlying passions and an expressive nature.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P10](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0010), [v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006), [v4 c24 P7](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0007), [v4 c25 P13](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0013), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c26 P5](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0005), [v4 c38 P33](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0033)_

- To capture the central idea for and write a great Canadian novel  <sub>[v4 c23 P18](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0018), [v4 c23 P20](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0020)</sub>
- To write Captain Jim's life story into a book  <sub>[v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)</sub>

## History

After recovering from typhoid, Owen Ford traveled to Four Winds on his doctor's orders and boarded at the house among the willows with Leslie Moore. He visited Anne Blythe and Captain Jim, who showed him his "life-book." Recognizing its potential, Owen collaborated with Captain Jim during the summer to weave the sea captain's life story and the romance of lost Margaret into a novel. Throughout the summer, he fell deeply in love with Leslie, but believing she was bound to her invalid husband, he kept his feelings secret and left Four Winds distraught after completing his manuscript. After Dick Moore's true identity was discovered and Leslie was freed, Owen returned to Four Winds the following August. He proposed to Leslie in Anne's garden, crowning her hair with a red rose, and she accepted. His novel, titled The Life-Book of Captain Jim, was published to great success in the autumn, and he arranged to purchase the house of dreams to use for summer vacations.

## Background by volume

- Son of Alice Selwyn and an Ontario man named Ford  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c24 P22](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0022)</sub>
- Grandson of John Selwyn, the schoolmaster who built the house among the willows  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- Grandson of Persis Selwyn, the schoolmaster's bride  <sub>[v4 c24 P19](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0019), [v4 c24 P21](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0021)</sub>
- Suffered from a severe spell of typhoid in the spring prior to visiting Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’ve never been able to get the right central idea for it. It lurks beyond me—it allures—and beckons—and recedes—I almost grasp it and it is gone. Perhaps amid this peace and loveliness, I shall be able to capture it.  <sub>[v4 c23 P20](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0020)</sub>

> We’ll collaborate. You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work.  <sub>[v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)</sub>

> Mrs. Blythe, I love Leslie. LOVE her! That seems too weak a word!  <sub>[v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)</sub>

> Perhaps, it is the prisoned infinite in us calling out to its kindred infinite as expressed in that visible perfection.  <sub>[v4 c26 P24](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0024)</sub>

> Yes—love triumphant and perfect. Leslie, you know—you understand. I have loved you from the first. And I KNOW you love me—I don’t need to ask you. But I want to hear you say it—my darling—my darling!  <sub>[v4 c38 P9](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0009)</sub>
